hint.text: Distance-time graphs are a specific form of line graphs. These graphs show how the distance and speed of an object/person (Lola, in this case) changes over time. The steepness of the line represents the speed at which Lola is moving.

instruction.text: This line graph shows the distance Lola covered on her journey home from school and how long it took her. Look at the line graph and answer the questions.

atoms.a: What is the distance between Lola’s house and the tree?
Between which two points did Lola run? Look for where she was travelling the fastest.

hint.text: On a distance-time graph, the steeper the line, the faster the movement. Look for where the line is steepest to see when Lola ran.

atoms.b: She ran between ((++the_church ++the_tree the_house)) and ((++the_church ++the_tree the_house)).

atoms.a: How far did she run between the church and the tree?
At which point did Lola stop for a rest?

hint.text: On a distance-time graph, when the line is flat, there is no movement. Look for where the line is flat to see when Lola stopped for a rest.

atoms.a: How long did she rest for?
